chunks.text: 69-year-old male, Retired, resident of Jurong West, Singapore.
Elective total hip replacement (THR) due to osteoarthritis (elective).
General anesthesia with spinal anesthesia as co-anesthesia, with ultrasound-guided peripheral nerve block for postoperative pain management

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms./Mrs. [Last Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your upcoming total hip replacement surgery. I'd like to go through some questions to ensure your safety and comfort during the procedure. Is that okay with you?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. I'm ready. I want to make sure everything goes smoothly for my hip surgery.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Let's start with your current health. You're having this surgery for osteoarthritis, particularly in your left hip. Can you tell me a bit about your symptoms and how they've been affecting your daily life?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure, doctor. My left hip has been really painful, especially when I walk or stand for too long. It's been getting worse over the past couple of years. I can't even climb stairs properly anymore, so I'm hoping this surgery will help me move around better.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. Now, let's go over your medications. I see you're on Atorvastatin, Metformin, Losartan, Aspirin, and Ranitidine. Have there been any changes to your medication list in the last 12 months, particularly regarding medications for stomach acid or ulcer prevention?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Ah, yes, doctor. I actually stopped taking Ranitidine about six months ago because I heard there were concerns about some contamination issues. My family doctor switched me to Omeprazole 20 mg daily instead for my stomach protection.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for letting me know. That's very important. Are you currently taking all your other medications as prescribed, including Aspirin, which we usually continue up to the day of surgery for patients like you with cardiovascular considerations?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. I take all my medications regularly, including the Aspirin. I haven't missed any doses.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Now, regarding allergies, I see you have a rash to Penicillin. Have you had any other allergic reactions to medications, foods, or latex that I should be aware of?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. Just that one reaction to Penicillin when I was younger. No issues with anything else.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to know. Let's talk about your medical history. You have Hypertension, Type 2 Diabetes, and Stage 3 Chronic Kidney Disease. How well are these conditions controlled? Have you had any recent complications or hospitalizations?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: My blood pressure and sugar levels have been pretty stable, doctor. I check my blood sugar regularly and it's within the target range. My kidney function is monitored, and while it's not perfect, it hasn't gotten worse recently. No hospitalizations in the past year.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's reassuring. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? If so, were there any complications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I had a cataract surgery a few years back, and that went smoothly. No issues with the anesthesia at all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Now, regarding your fasting status for surgery: when was the last time you had food and drink?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I had dinner around 7 PM last night and a small sip of water with my morning medications at 6 AM this morning. Nothing else since then.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect, thank you. Finally, I'd like to outline the anesthesia plan for you. We're planning for General Anesthesia with Spinal Anesthesia as a co-anesthesia. Additionally, we'll be performing an Ultrasound-Guided Peripheral Nerve Block for postoperative pain management. This should help keep you comfortable after surgery. Do you have any questions about this plan?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. It sounds like a good plan. I'm just looking forward to having my hip fixed and being able to walk without so much pain.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I'm glad to hear that. If any questions come up before surgery, don't hesitate to reach out. We're here to ensure the best possible outcome for you.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] spinal anesthesia administered, twenty five milligrams of bupivacaine

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] ultrasound-guided peripheral nerve block, ten milliliters of ropivacaine

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] hypotension noted, mean arterial pressure forty five mmHg, one milligram of phenylephrine administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [09:00] two liters of lactated ringers administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [09:20] tachycardia noted, heart rate one twenty beats per minute, incremental dose of fentanyl twenty five micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm okay, doctor. A bit sleepy, but not in too much pain.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. Can you tell me your pain level on a scale from 0 to 10, where 0 is no pain and 10 is the worst?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'd say about a 3. The nerve block seems to be helping a lot.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Are you feeling nauseous or have been sick at all since waking up?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, no nausea. I feel fine in that way.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. How about your breathing? Any discomfort or difficulty breathing?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I'm breathing fine. Chest feels okay.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Do you remember anything about the surgery itself? Any awareness during the procedure?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don't remember anything. I was out the whole time.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's expected with general anesthesia. Given your diabetes and kidney condition, we'll keep a close eye on your fluids and blood sugar levels. Any other concerns from your side?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. Thank you for checking on me.

Intraoperative course included general anesthesia with spinal and ultrasound-guided peripheral nerve block. Notable events: hypotension (MAP 45 mmHg) and tachycardia (HR 120 bpm) requiring interventions. Postoperatively, anticipate risks for PONV, airway complications, glycemic control issues, analgesia management challenges, hemodynamic instability, AKI, and increased bleeding risk due to Aspirin.

Monitor for PONV, airway complications, and glycemic control. Carefully titrate analgesics to avoid under/over-treatment. Watch for hemodynamic instability and signs of AKI. Manage bleeding risk with caution. Continue current medications as ordered, and maintain NPO status until further notice.
